label: STOPP C2: blood thinner with high bleeding risk
title: Antiplatelet or anticoagulant with a high risk of major bleeding
statement: Antiplatelet agents, vitamin K antagonists, direct thrombin inhibitors or factor Xa inhibitors with concurrent significant risk of major bleeding, i.e. uncontrolled severe hypertension, bleeding diathesis, recent non-trivial spontaneous bleeding (high risk of bleeding).

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)

plain_summary: A blood-thinning medicine given to a person with severe uncontrolled high blood pressure, a bleeding disorder or a recent bleed that was not trivial carries a high risk of serious bleeding.

medicine_groups.name: Antiplatelet medicines
medicine_groups.note: Aspirin counts only as a low dose taken daily as an antiplatelet, for example 100 mg. Aspirin used only for pain does not count. A prescribed fraction of a higher-strength tablet counts when the dose and directions support daily antiplatelet use. Asasantin SR is aspirin with dipyridamole. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too. CoPlavix, DuoCover, DuoPlidogrel, Piax Plus Aspirin and Clopidogrel/Aspirin 75/100 (APX) contain clopidogrel with aspirin. One such tablet supplies both antiplatelet ingredients. For aspirin alone, verify the dose and daily antiplatelet use before counting an ambiguous brand.

medicine_groups.name: Warfarin, dabigatran and the factor Xa inhibitors
medicine_groups.note: Warfarin is the vitamin K antagonist. Dabigatran is the direct thrombin inhibitor. Apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban and fondaparinux are factor Xa inhibitors. No Australian brand is listed for edoxaban. Fondaparinux is an injection. Heparin and enoxaparin are not in this group. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

rule_for_models: For people aged 65 or older, assess Group A or B supplies in the last six months counted back from the latest date in the record. Count aspirin when its strength and directions support daily antiplatelet use, including a prescribed tablet fraction. Exclude aspirin taken only for pain. Use quantity and daily dose to find the covered dates, or the dated schedule for a variable dose. Confirm a finding if any one risk qualifies: a bleeding disorder during exposure, repeated readings during exposure that each show systolic pressure of at least 180 mmHg or diastolic pressure of at least 110 mmHg, or significant spontaneous bleeding during exposure or in the preceding six months. A pharmacist answer that confirms the risk for that period counts. A negative answer excludes only that risk. If none qualifies and a risk or its timing is unknown, report a possible finding. Name each missing fact exactly as listed: "Repeated blood pressure readings during antiplatelet or anticoagulant exposure", "Bleeding disorder during blood-thinner treatment", or "Significant spontaneous bleeding during blood-thinner treatment or in the six months before it". One reading alone or uncertain overlap leaves the blood pressure pattern unknown. Refer uncertain dose or exposure to the pharmacist without assuming coverage from refills. If all three risks are excluded, report no finding. Unknown age means unknown eligibility. For every finding, cite a qualifying supply. For a confirmed finding, also cite the dated risk evidence: the bleeding disorder or bleed line, both qualifying blood pressure readings, or the pharmacist assessment confirming the risk during the relevant period.

needs_facts.what: Repeated blood pressure readings during antiplatelet or anticoagulant exposure
needs_facts.meets: Repeated readings during exposure show systolic pressure of at least 180 mmHg or diastolic pressure of at least 110 mmHg. One isolated high reading without follow-up leaves this risk uncertain.

options.words: Repeated readings during exposure each showed systolic pressure of at least 180 mmHg or diastolic pressure of at least 110 mmHg
Repeat readings during exposure did not show this severe pattern
Only one relevant reading is available
Readings or overlap with treatment not known

needs_facts.meets: A bleeding disorder was present during exposure. A disorder confined to a different period does not meet this risk.

needs_facts.what: Significant spontaneous bleeding during blood-thinner treatment or in the six months before it
needs_facts.meets: A non-trivial spontaneous bleed occurred during the exposure being assessed or in the preceding six months. A dated entry or explicit confirmation of timing is sufficient.

options.words: A significant spontaneous bleed occurred in that period
No significant spontaneous bleed in that period

cannot_be_seen: Blood pressure at home or at the surgery, bleeding that was never recorded, results such as platelet counts, and why the blood thinner was started. Also medicines supplied by a hospital or another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: Could we review the bleeding risk today if the patient is still taking the medicine and a significant risk is present? Where a risk or its timing is unknown, could you confirm it and review the balance of benefit and harm?
